noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

retryable.description: Retry action if failure is a retryable c3 exception such as VersionConflict.

class.description: The class name of the native field type, parameter or return value (as marked with the "native" value type).

sourceVersion.description:
Specific version of the language required for the source code. The supported versions vary by language so for
languages that support multiple versions, this field is overridden with an enumeration. If unspecified, it is
assumed that the source code corresponds to a "base" version which is upward compatible.

typeSystem.description:
Whether the C3 type system is required.  Off by default, this can be enabled if
the C3 type system is needed.  This will also result in loading the types for the
current env and app.

If not enabled, the local C3 type system is not available and no calls may
be made back to the server.

customRuntime.description:
True if this method can support custom runtimes, other than the one it claims. This is used for special cases
such as tester endpoints where the runtime isn't known at authoring time.

title:
Actions (type methods) implemented in JavaScript run as an external Node.js process. This allows specification
of packages available through NPM so as to easily use third-party libraries in action implementations.

A Node.js app built with these dependencies:

```json
{
  "name": "example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "an example app",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "async": "^2.1.4",
    "request": "^2.79.0"
  }
}
```

Can be implemented by associating the source code (contents of `index.js`) with the type action function.
For example, if the type name "Example" and the function name was "example", the code in `Example.js`
must implement a function named "example" that implements the behavior of the action function.

Note that multiple functions on the type may be implemented by Node.js, each as a separate JavaScript
function in the same type-specific file (`Example.js`).

Then the NPM dependencies are bundled into a named set and defined on the containing C3 metadata package as
a distinct "runtime". For example, the NPM dependencies above might be used to define a new runtime
in metadata dir, e.g. metadata/ImplLanguage.Runtime/js-node-example.json:

```json
{
  "id": "js-node-example",
  "name": "js-node-example",
  "language": "JavaScript",
  "runtime": "Node.js",
  "modules": {
    "async": "^2.1.4",
    "request": "^2.79.0"
  }
}
```

By default, the "js-node.json" environment is used, which must also be defined by the C3 metadata package.
The runtime can be associated with the explicit syntax:

```c3typ
  example: function(arg: string): string js node-example
```

@see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js
@see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Npm_(software)
